To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the subfossil Eastern Red Cedar stumps are the remains of a coastal forest that existed in a back-barrior setting; 2) the stumps were drowned by episodic storms and moderate rates of relative sea-level rise during the past millennium; and 3) future increases in sea-level rise and storm events will lead to the rapid destruction of terrestrial ecosystems along the Atlantic coast of North America.
